the elucidation of the molecular basis of protein synthesis.
the study of the structure and function of the ribosome.

the ribosomal binding sites for the elongation factors EF-G and EF-Tu are located in the 30 S subunit, and that the binding sites for EF-Tu and EF-G are not identical.
L28 (L1, L3 and LI4) and L23 are in the neighbourhood, or at the ribosomal binding surface for EF-Tu.
the proteins L23, LI and L3 are located in the vicinity of the binding site on the ribosomal 50 S subunit for the elongation factors Tu and G.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ribosomal protein L23 is located at the ribosomal binding sites for both the elongation factors EF-G and EF-Tu.
the proteins L23, and L24 are located in the neighborhood of the binding site of the EF-Tu.
we have found that EF-Tu binds to ribosomes at a site which is in the neighbourhood of proteins L23, 28, Ll, L3, and L24.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EF-Tu binding site on the ribosome has a very high affinity for EF-Tu, and that this binding is not affected by the presence of EF-G or GTP.
the ribosome is an incredibly complex machine, and that it’s not enough to just study the structure of the ribosome to understand its function.
